mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: An object at rest will stay at rest unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.B: A moving object will continue moving at constant speed in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.C: A stationary object needs a force to keep it moving.
options.D: In the absence of net external force, the velocity of an object remains unchanged.

mcqs.answer: A stationary object needs a force to keep it moving.
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that a force is required to keep an object moving. Newton's first law states that an object in motion continues in uniform motion unless a net external force acts on it; no continuous force is needed to maintain motion. Options A, B, and D correctly describe the law, while option C is the false belief.

mcqs.question: Which everyday situation best illustrates Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: A book resting on a table.
options.B: A car accelerating when the driver presses the gas pedal.
options.C: A ball rolling on a frictionless surface continues moving at constant speed in a straight line.
options.D: A skydiver reaching terminal velocity during free fall.

mcqs.answer: A ball rolling on a frictionless surface continues moving at constant speed in a straight line.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law states that an object in motion remains in motion with constant velocity unless acted upon by an external force. In option C, the only force that could change the motion (friction) is absent, so the ball maintains its state of motion, directly demonstrating the law. The other options involve either no motion or external forces causing acceleration.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines inertia?

options.A: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion; it is directly proportional to its mass.
options.B: Inertia is the force exerted by an object due to its motion.
options.C: Inertia is the same as weight, which depends on the gravitational field.
options.D: Inertia is the acceleration produced by a net external force.

mcqs.answer: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion; it is directly proportional to its mass.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is a property of matter that quantifies its resistance to any change in its velocity (including direction). It is directly related to mass: more massive objects have greater inertia. Options B, C, and D describe different concepts (force, weight, and acceleration) and are incorrect.

mcqs.question: A 5 kg block rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. Which statement about its inertia of rest is correct?

options.A: It will remain at rest until a net external force acts on it.
options.B: It will start moving spontaneously due to its inertia.
options.C: Its inertia is zero because it is not moving.
options.D: Its inertia depends on the roughness of the surface.

mcqs.answer: It will remain at rest until a net external force acts on it.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest is the tendency of a stationary object to stay stationary. According to Newton's first law, the block will not move unless a net external force is applied. Options B and C misinterpret inertia, and D incorrectly links inertia to surface texture.

mcqs.question: What does the term 'inertia of motion' refer to?

options.A: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving at the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
options.B: The tendency of a moving object to stop moving unless a force is continuously applied.
options.C: The resistance of a material to being deformed under stress.
options.D: The dependence of an object's weight on the gravitational field.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving at the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion describes the resistance of a moving body to any change in its velocity. It is precisely the content of Newton's first law. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated phenomena.

mcqs.question: Inertia of direction means that an object in motion tends to:

options.B: Continue moving in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.C: Accelerate in the direction of any applied force.

mcqs.answer: Continue moving in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: The 'direction' aspect of inertia states that, without a net external force, an object's velocity vector (both magnitude and direction) remains unchanged, so it moves in a straight line. Option A contradicts the law, while C and D describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: Select the statement that correctly states Newton's first law of motion and distinguishes it from other laws.

options.A: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.B: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and occurs in the direction of the force.
options.C: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: Option A precisely expresses Newton's first law (law of inertia) and differentiates it from the second law (option B), third law (option C), and the formulaic expression of the second law (option D). The other options describe different laws.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday application of Newton's first law?

options.A: A ball thrown upward returns to the ground.
options.B: A car stopping abruptly when the brakes are applied.
options.C: A book sliding on a table continues moving after the push stops, if friction is negligible.

mcqs.answer: A book sliding on a table continues moving after the push stops, if friction is negligible.
mcqs.explanation: When friction is negligible, the book experiences no net external force after the push, so it maintains its state of motion, illustrating Newton's first law. Options A and B involve external forces (gravity, braking), and D involves continuous muscular force, none of which directly demonstrate the law.
